startup_rule: Prefer the newest verified portable state/checkpoint artifact from current chat, Project Sources or Library.
Consult PROJECT-STATE.json and the relevant GitHub CHECKPOINT.json only as much as needed to resolve ambiguity or sync status.
Read README.md, Prompt/START-PROMPT-v3.1.12.md, SOURCE-ACCESS-PROTOCOL-v1.0.0.md and SOURCE-REGISTRY.json when their rules are relevant.
Resolve registered raw sources from Project Sources first, then Library; do not ask the user to re-upload until both have been checked.
Inspect German-Flashcards-Pro only when runtime/import/presentation compatibility actually matters.

authority_resolution.user_supplied_newer_artifact: Immediate working authority when explicitly identified as current/latest.
authority_resolution.portable_verified_state: Preferred resume authority after an explicit current artifact; may live in current conversation, Project Sources or Library.
authority_resolution.github: Durable asynchronous checkpoint/coordination mirror, not a blocker and not the default binary transport.
authority_resolution.conflict_rule: Never silently replace newer verified work with older GitHub content. Mark Git sync pending instead.
authority_resolution.persistence_rule: Synchronize Git at meaningful boundaries. Git lag must not block ordinary safe work. Do not call a result Git-backed PASS/FINAL/VERIFIED until that persistence is complete.

workstream_resolution_policy: Use the newest verified portable workstream checkpoint first. Git branch checkpoint remains the durable mirror and ambiguity resolver; its stage observation may lag parallel work.
